stages.name: Outside the war
stages.desc: Lands that kept out of the fighting, or were only drawn in at the edges

stages.name: Athens and its empire
stages.desc: Athens, its tribute-paying allies and its bases

stages.name: Sparta and its allies
stages.desc: Sparta, Corinth, Thebes and the Peloponnesian League

stages.name: In revolt from Athens
stages.desc: Allies who broke away, or were won over by Brasidas

stages.name: Socrates in the field
stages.desc: Where Socrates fought as a hoplite, in the years he was there

states.name: West Macedonia
timeline: Upper Macedonia: the hill kingdoms of Lyncus and Elimeia
Brasidas and King Perdiccas campaign against Arrhabaeus of Lyncus and fall out

states.name: Epirus
timeline: The Molossians and other peoples of Epirus, outside the war

states.name: Centre Macedonia
timeline: Potidaea revolts from Athens; Socrates is in the army that fights before its walls and besieges it
Winter 430/429: starving Potidaea surrenders after a siege that cost Athens 2,000 talents
The Chalcidian cities hold out and beat an Athenian army at Spartolus
The Spartan Brasidas wins over Acanthus and Stagirus and takes Amphipolis by surprise
Cleon's army, Socrates in it, is routed at Amphipolis; Cleon and Brasidas are both killed

states.name: East Macedonia and Thrace
timeline: Thasos and the Thracian coast, rich in silver and timber, pay tribute to Athens
Thucydides, general at Thasos, sails to save Amphipolis and arrives too late

states.name: Mount Athos
timeline: The small towns of the Athos peninsula pay tribute to Athens
Most of the Athos towns go over to Brasidas

states.name: Thessalia
timeline: Thessaly's horse-breeding aristocracies, allied to Athens on paper
Brasidas marches quickly through Thessaly on his way to Thrace

states.name: Central Greece
timeline: Boeotia, led by Thebes, is Sparta's ally; Euboea pays tribute to Athens
A Theban night attack on Plataea opens the war
Plataea surrenders; the Spartans put its defenders to death
Delium: the Boeotians rout the Athenians; Socrates is in the retreat
The Boeotians hold Delium and keep the Athenians out

states.name: Attica
timeline: Athens bans Megara from its markets; Sparta's allies demand war
A Spartan army ravages Attica; the country people crowd inside the walls
Plague breaks out in the crowded city
Pericles dies of the plague
Spartan prisoners from Pylos are held in Athens; the invasions stop
Aristophanes' Clouds mocks Socrates on the Athenian stage

states.name: Peloponnese
timeline: Sparta and its Peloponnesian League vote that Athens has broken the peace; Argos stays neutral
At Pylos, in Messenia, Athens traps and captures 292 men, about 120 of them Spartans

states.name: West Greece
timeline: Athens' base at Naupactus and its Acarnanian allies; Elis, to the south, fights for Sparta
Phormio's small Athenian squadron beats larger Peloponnesian fleets off Naupactus
Demosthenes is beaten in the Aetolian hills

states.name: South Aegean
timeline: The Cyclades pay tribute to Athens; Melos, a Spartan colony, stays apart
Athens purifies the sacred island of Delos

states.name: North Aegean
timeline: Lesbos, Chios and Lemnos: Athens' strongest allies, with fleets of their own
Mytilene leads Lesbos in revolt
Mytilene surrenders; Athens votes to kill its men, then sends a second ship to cancel the order

states.name: Ionian Islands
timeline: The Ionian islands: Corcyra, Athens' ally since 433, and Cephallenia, won over in 431
Civil war on Corcyra between democrats and oligarchs

events.title: Megarian decree
events.text: Athens shuts Megara out of the harbours and markets of its empire.

events.title: Sparta votes war
events.text: The Spartan assembly votes that Athens has broken the Thirty Years' Peace.

events.title: Potidaea revolts
events.text: Potidaea, a Corinthian colony in Athens' empire, breaks away with Macedonian encouragement.

events.title: Aristeus arrives
events.text: The Corinthian Aristeus brings 1,600 hoplites and 400 light troops to defend Potidaea.

events.title: Battle before Potidaea
events.text: Athens wins on the isthmus; 150 Athenians and their general Callias die. Socrates fights there.

events.title: The walls close
events.text: Phormio walls off Potidaea from the Pallene side; the city is under siege.

events.title: Plataea attacked
events.text: A Theban night attack on Athens' ally Plataea begins the war.

events.title: Attica invaded
events.text: King Archidamus' army burns the farms around Acharnae.

events.title: Barefoot on the ice
events.text: In a winter of hard frost, Plato says, Socrates walked over the ice barefoot.

events.title: Standing all night
events.text: One summer day, Plato says, Socrates stood thinking from dawn to the next dawn.

events.title: The plague
events.text: Plague breaks out first in Piraeus, then in the crowded city.

events.title: Plague at Potidaea
events.text: Fresh troops bring the plague: 1,050 of 4,000 hoplites die in forty days.

events.title: Potidaea surrenders
events.text: In the winter of 430/429, after the starving people have eaten one another, Potidaea gives in.

events.title: Pericles dies
events.text: Athens' leading statesman dies of the plague.

events.title: Spartolus
events.text: The Chalcidians beat an Athenian army and kill its generals.

events.title: Phormio's victories
events.text: Twenty Athenian ships beat larger Peloponnesian fleets off Naupactus.

events.title: Mytilene revolts
events.text: The cities of Lesbos, except Methymna, break away from Athens.

events.title: Plato is born
events.text: Plato is born in Athens in 428 or 427, four years before Delium.

events.title: The Mytilene debate
events.text: The Athenians vote to kill all of Mytilene's men, then repent and send a second ship.

events.title: Plataea falls
events.text: The last defenders surrender and are put to death by the Spartans.

events.title: Gorgias in Athens
events.text: The orator Gorgias dazzles the Assembly as an envoy from Leontini.

events.title: Tanagra
events.text: An Athenian army defeats the Tanagraeans and their Theban allies.

events.title: Aetolia
events.text: Demosthenes' army is cut to pieces in the Aetolian hills.

events.title: Pylos and Sphacteria
events.text: Athens captures 292 men, about 120 of them Spartans, on the island of Sphacteria.

events.title: Delium fortified
events.text: Hippocrates fortifies the sanctuary of Apollo at Delium, on the Boeotian coast.

events.title: Battle of Delium
events.text: The Boeotians rout the Athenians; nearly 1,000 hoplites die. Socrates is in the retreat.

events.title: Delium burned
events.text: With a fire-blowing device, the Boeotians retake Delium seventeen days later.

events.title: Brasidas in Thessaly
events.text: The Spartan Brasidas slips through Thessaly with 1,700 hoplites.

events.title: Acanthus won over
events.text: Brasidas persuades Acanthus to leave Athens' empire.

events.title: Amphipolis falls
events.text: In a winter snowstorm, Brasidas takes Athens' colony on the Strymon.

events.title: Thucydides at Eion
events.text: The general Thucydides saves only Eion and is exiled; he writes the war's history.

events.title: The Clouds
events.text: Aristophanes mocks Socrates as a crank in a basket; the play comes third.

events.title: Truce for a year
events.text: Athens and Sparta agree a truce, but Scione revolts two days later.

events.title: Mende revolts
events.text: Mende goes over to Brasidas; the Athenians retake it in the summer.

events.title: Torone retaken
events.text: Cleon storms Torone and sends its men to Athens as prisoners.

events.title: Cleon at Eion
events.text: Cleon waits at Eion with 1,200 Athenian hoplites, 300 horse and allies.

events.title: Battle of Amphipolis
events.text: Brasidas' sally routs Cleon's army; about 600 Athenians die, and seven on his side.

events.title: Two generals dead
events.text: Cleon is killed in flight; Brasidas, mortally wounded, lives to hear of his victory.

events.title: Brasidas the founder
events.text: Amphipolis buries Brasidas in its market place and honours him as its founder.

chartNote: Share of the area of thirteen modern Greek regions (Crete is left out), by each region's side in the war's first ten years and by where Socrates fought. Regions are today's boundaries, and a whole region takes the colour of its leading cities: Boeotia shares one with Athenian Euboea, Attica includes Megara. A simplification; dates are approximate turning points.
